s: A company runs an IoT application that consists of many connected IoT sensors. The company runs Eclipse Mosquitto MQTT brokers on two Amazon EC2 instances. The MQTT brokers send incoming data to a processing service that runs on a separate set of two EC2 instances that is the target for an Application Load Balancer (ALB). On average, the MQTT message rate is 1,500 messages each second. Surges of MQTT messages occur at unpredictable times throughout each day. Message surges can involve up to three times the average amount of traffic. The Mosquitto MQTT brokers cannot handle the increased number of connections. The company needs a solution to improve the application's scalability. Which solution will meet this requirement?
o: Migrate the MQTT brokers to AWS IoT Core. Create an AWS IoT rule to invoke an AWS Step Functions Express state machine to process data.
Migrate the MQTT brokers to AWS IoT Core. Create an AWS IoT rule to send incoming data to an Amazon EventBridge pipe. Invoke an AWS Lambda function from the pipe to process data.
Update the IoT sensors to send data to Amazon Data Firehose. Configure Firehose to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process data.
Update the IoT sensors to send data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure the data stream to invoke a new AWS Step Functions state machine to process data.
e: Option A is correct because AWS IoT Core is a managed MQTT broker service built to handle large scale device connectivity and message ingestion without the company managing Mosquitto brokers on EC2. AWS IoT rules can process MQTT topic messages and route them to AWS services, including AWS Step Functions. A Step Functions Express workflow is suitable for high-volume, event-driven processing because it is designed for short-duration, high-throughput workflows. Option B is not the best fit because EventBridge Pipes is not the direct AWS IoT rules action pattern required here. Option C requires changing devices to send data to Firehose instead of MQTT. Option D also requires device-side protocol changes and does not provide the managed MQTT connectivity layer that solves the broker scalability problem.

w.y: The brokers can't handle surges in connections, so the fix is a managed MQTT broker that scales: AWS IoT Core. An IoT rule can start a Step Functions Express workflow directly to process each message.

o.A: Correct: IoT Core replaces the brokers and an IoT rule triggers a Step Functions Express workflow.
o.B: IoT rules cannot target an EventBridge pipe directly; pipes read from sources such as SQS or Kinesis.
o.C: Sensors would need to be changed to send to Firehose, which is not an MQTT endpoint, and Firehose transformation is not meant for this processing.
o.D: Kinesis Data Streams cannot invoke Step Functions directly, and sensors would need to be rewritten.
